chunks: They both said: We asked him about a man who struck a man with a stick and did not stop until he died. Should he be handed over to the guardian of the slain one so that he may kill him? He said: Yes, and he should not be left to abuse him with it, but rather the sword should be used upon him.

key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْمَقْتُولِ: The guardian or next-of-kin of the slain person, who holds the right to exact retaliation (qisas) or accept blood money (diyya)
key_terms.يَعْبَثُ: To play with, abuse, or torment — here indicating the prohibition against using the same cruel method (stick beating) for execution
key_terms.يُجِيزُ عَلَيْهِ بِالسَّيْفِ: To execute with the sword — the lawful and dignified method of carrying out the death penalty in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Islam when a man beats another to death with a stick — is qisas applicable and how should it be carried out?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on a case of intentional killing by repeated beating with a stick. The Imam affirms that the killer (qisas) right belongs to the next-of-kin of the slain, but specifies that retaliation must be carried out with the sword — not by the same abusive method used in the killing. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle of proportionality in qisas while preserving the dignity of the condemned and preventing unnecessary suffering.
